scope_note: Released feature-film acting appearances by Shashi Kapoor (18 March 1938 – 4 December 2017), whose acting career runs from the child role in Aag (1948) to Ghar Bazar (1998). Includes lead, co-lead, supporting and antagonist roles, cameos and guest appearances, appearances as himself, narration, child roles, and his English-language work for Merchant Ivory and others (The Householder, Shakespeare Wallah, Pretty Polly, Bombay Talkie, Siddhartha, Heat and Dust, Sammy and Rosie Get Laid, The Deceivers, In Custody, Jinnah, Side Streets). Excluded: seven titles the Wikipedia filmography marks unreleased (Jise Tu Kabool Kar Le, Ek Do Teen Chaar, Pyar To Hona Hi Tha, Do Guru, Chakma, Bandh Honth, Apna Ghar); films he produced or directed without acting (36 Chowringhee Lane, 1981; Ajooba, 1991; the Soviet version Vozvrashcheniye Bagdadskogo Vora, 1988); his assistant-director credits (Post Box 999, Guest House, Shriman Satyawadi, Dulha Dulhan, Manoranjan); and television, including the miniseries Gulliver's Travels (1996), in which he played the Rajah. Bachpan (1945) is excluded: its cast lists a 'Shashi Kapoor', but the film is a Basant Pictures production of Homi Wadia and the credit belongs to the older same-named child actor of mythologicals, billed 'Shashi Kapoor Sr.', whom Kapoor's own article cites as the reason he was billed 'Shashiraj' as a child. Samadhi (1950) is included although the Wikipedia filmography table omits it, because the Shashi Kapoor article's career section names it among his child-artist films and the film article casts him as Pratap, the young brother of Ashok Kumar's Shekhar; the same article's early-life section says he made four child films, which conflicts, and with Samadhi the count is five. Release dates are Indian theatrical dates where the film article gives them, otherwise the year. Four films sit in a different year from the one the filmography table gives, each noted on the row: Jahan Pyar Mile (article title Jahan Pyar Miley, released 30 October 1970), Rootha Na Karo (infobox 31 December 1969 against a 1970 year in both the article text and the filmography table), Touhean (completed 1987, released 20 November 1992) and In Custody (Tokyo Film Festival, October 1993, with 1994 New York and London releases). Box-office figures without a nett/gross label are kept in research notes rather than in the money columns. Films without a Wikipedia article rest on the filmography table alone and are graded accordingly; two of them, Swayamvar (1980) and Ek Aur Ek Gyaarah (1981), are linked in that table to the biographies of Moushumi Chatterjee and Vinod Khanna rather than to film articles, which is an error on Wikipedia's side.

career_phases.summary: Billed as Shashiraj to avoid confusion with an older actor of the same name, Kapoor plays the child version of his brother Raj Kapoor's characters in Aag and Awaara and of Ashok Kumar's in Sangram, alongside Samadhi and Daana Paani. These are family-firm appearances arranged around Prithvi Theatres rather than a career, and they carry no romantic content.

Kapoor returns as an adult lead in Yash Chopra's partition drama Dharmputra and in Char Diwari, both commercial failures, followed by modest successes in Bimal Roy's Prem Patra and Yeh Dil Kisko Doon. The period also opens the parallel English-language career that runs beside the Hindi one for thirty years, beginning with James Ivory's The Householder (1963).

Waqt and Jab Jab Phool Khile, both released in 1965, make him a star; the latter wins him the BFJA Best Actor award and fixes the gentle, courteous romantic persona that the project's romance scoring is largely built to measure. Hits with Kanyadaan, Haseena Maan Jayegi, Sharmeelee and Aa Gale Lag Jaa follow, opposite Nanda, Asha Parekh, Babita, Rakhee and Sharmila Tagore, while Shakespeare Wallah, Bombay Talkie and Siddhartha run the art-cinema track in parallel.

career_phases.phase: Peak commercial years and the multi-starrer
career_phases.summary: Chor Machaye Shor and Roti Kapada Aur Makaan take the top two box-office places of 1974 and make him one of the most saleable stars of the decade. The defining pattern is the multi-starrer, above all opposite Amitabh Bachchan in Deewaar (Filmfare Best Supporting Actor), Kabhi Kabhie, Immaan Dharam, Trishul, Kaala Patthar, Suhaag, Shaan, Silsila and Namak Halaal, where his function is frequently the lawful or forgiving brother and romance is subordinate to the male pairing. He simultaneously funds a parallel-cinema slate through Film-Valas, producing and starring in Junoon and Kalyug and producing 36 Chowringhee Lane and Vijeta.

career_phases.phase: Parallel cinema, character roles and decline
career_phases.summary: Star power wanes after 1982 and Kapoor shifts toward prestige and character work: Utsav, which he also produced, and New Delhi Times, which brings the National Film Award for Best Actor and a second BFJA award. He takes supporting and cameo parts in mainstream films (Ghar Ek Mandir, Ilzaam, Ijaazat, Sindoor, his last box-office success), continues the English-language line with Heat and Dust, Sammy and Rosie Get Laid and The Deceivers, and directs Ajooba in 1991.

Work thins to a handful of late and delayed releases. In Custody brings a National Film Award Special Jury recognition, and the career closes in 1998 with the narrator of Jinnah, a cameo in Swami Vivekananda, Side Streets and the long-delayed Ghar Bazar, after which he stops acting. Lifetime honours follow in retirement: the Filmfare Lifetime Achievement Award in 2010, the Padma Bhushan in 2011 and the Dadasaheb Phalke Award in 2015.
